parts.title: Multiple choice (Questions 1–50)
parts.instructions: This paper has 50 multiple choice questions (1 to 50). Each question has 4 choices. Choose ONE best answer and blacken its letter on the separate answer sheet.

source.document: raw/2019_Science__V-A.pdf (8 pages: cover + questions on pp. 2-8, 'THE END' after Q50)
source.notes: Cover: 'Eritrean Grade 8 National Examinations 2019 – 4-Science – Version-A'. Only Version A is available. Text from the PDF text layer, checked against the page images. The text layer also contains a hidden line 'TIME ALLOWED: 1 hour and 40 minutes (100 minutes)'. The visible cover shows 1 hour and 10 minutes (70 minutes), which is used here. Figures cropped at 250 dpi: satellite orbit (Q4), periodic table (Q6-Q7), pie chart of air (Q11), salt and sugar plates (Q20), circuit with cell, switch and bulb (Q24), Celsius thermometer (Q34), four tools (Q44), food chain (Q47). Tables 1 and 2 (Q33, Q49) are typed as stem tables.
source.printing_note: Clean digital print. Degree signs print as a raised 0 ('680F'); written as °F/°C. Q24 options A and C are identical (both 'electrical → chemical → light and heat'). Q29 options A and D carry the unit m instead of s. Figure labels 'Sattelite' (Q4) and 'Hawk' (Q47) as printed.

exam.answer_key_note: No official key. Answers solved and checked against the Eritrean MoE Grade 6–8 textbooks.

questions.stem: In humans, sperm cells are produced inside
explanation_steps: In males, sperm cells are made in the testes.
The ovary makes egg cells (female); the pistil is part of a flower. Answer: C.
(textbook: Science Grade 7, p. 189)
questions.explain_simple: Sperm cells are made in the testes.
tips: Testes → sperm. Ovaries → eggs.

similar_questions.stem: Egg cells are produced in the
explanation_steps: The ovaries produce egg cells.

questions.stem: All substances are made up of
explanation_steps: The textbook says all living and non-living things, like rocks, soil, water and air, are made of atoms.
Only living things are made of cells. Answer: C.
questions.explain_simple: Everything is made of atoms.
tips: Atoms are the building blocks of all matter.

similar_questions.stem: The smallest particle of an element that shows its properties is
explanation_steps: An atom is the smallest particle of an element.

textbook_ref.subject: Science
textbook_ref.unit: Unit 3 – The Structure of the Atom

questions.stem: Which of the following are produced by meiosis type of cell division?
explanation_steps: Meiosis happens in the testes, ovaries and flowers. It makes sex cells (sperm, eggs, pollen).
Blood, bone and skin cells are body cells made by mitosis. Answer: C.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 134)
questions.explain_simple: Meiosis makes sex cells.
tips: Meiosis → sex cells (half chromosomes). Mitosis → body cells.

similar_questions.stem: Which cell is made by mitosis?
explanation_steps: A skin cell is a body cell, made by mitosis.

questions.stem: In figure 1 below, the force that enables the satellite to move around the earth is:
questions.image_alt: Figure 1: a satellite moving in an oval path around the earth; arrows show the direction of motion.
explanation_steps: All objects in the universe attract each other with a gravitational force.
The earth's gravity pulls the satellite towards it and keeps it moving in a path around the earth (like the moon). Answer: D.
(textbook: Science Grade 7, p. 151)
questions.explain_simple: Gravity pulls the satellite and keeps it going around the earth.
tips: Gravity keeps the moon and satellites in orbit.

similar_questions.stem: What keeps the planets moving around the sun?
explanation_steps: The sun's gravitational force holds the planets in their paths.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a mechanism of the human body regulation against heat gain?
explanation_steps: When the body gets too hot, blood vessels near the skin widen. More blood flows near the skin and heat is lost to the air.
Sweating also starts (not stops). Shivering and erect hairs are responses to COLD. Answer: D.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 35)
questions.explain_simple: When we are hot, blood vessels near the skin get wider to lose heat.
tips: Hot: sweat, vessels widen, hairs lie flat. Cold: shiver, vessels narrow, hairs stand up.

similar_questions.stem: What does the body do when it is too cold?

options.C: widens blood vessels near the skin

explanation_steps: Shivering makes heat in the muscles.

questions.stem: Answer questions 6 and 7 based on figure 2, the Periodic Table given below. Which of the following elements are nonmetals?
questions.image_alt: Figure 2: outline of the periodic table. Group I: H, Li, Na, K. Group II: Be, Mg, Ca. Groups III–VIII in periods 1–3: He; B, C, N, O, F, Ne; Al, Si, P, S, Cl, Ar. A thick step line starts under B and goes down to the right between the metals and the nonmetals.
explanation_steps: In the periodic table, metals are on the left and nonmetals are on the right of the thick step-shaped line.
F (fluorine) and Ar (argon) are on the far right: both are nonmetals.
Na, Mg, Li, Be and Ca are metals in groups I and II. Answer: B.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 93)
questions.explain_simple: F and Ar are on the right side of the table. They are nonmetals.
tips: Left side: metals. Right side (after the step line): nonmetals.

similar_questions.stem: Which element is a metal?
explanation_steps: K (potassium) is in group I on the left: a metal.

textbook_ref.subject: Science
textbook_ref.unit: Unit 4 – Chemical Reactions and the Periodic Table

questions.stem: Which pair of elements is categorized as metalloids?
questions.image_alt: The same periodic table as in Q6, with the thick step line starting under B and passing Si.
explanation_steps: Metalloids are the elements near the step-shaped (metalloid) line. They have properties of both metals and nonmetals.
In the figure the line runs past B (boron) and Si (silicon). Both are metalloids.
N, C, S and Cl are nonmetals; K is a metal. Answer: C.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 93; Science Grade 8, p. 94)
questions.explain_simple: Boron and silicon are next to the step line. They are metalloids.
tips: Metalloids: B, Si, Ge, As, Sb, Te (along the step line).

similar_questions.stem: Silicon is used in computer chips. It is a
explanation_steps: Silicon has properties of both metals and nonmetals: a metalloid.

questions.stem: Plant leaves wilt down when there is shortage of water in soil. So, the stimulus is
explanation_steps: A stimulus is a change in the environment that causes a response.
The change here is the shortage of water. The wilting of the leaves is the response. Answer: A.
(textbook: Science Grade 7, p. 79)
questions.explain_simple: The lack of water is the stimulus. Wilting is the response.
tips: Stimulus = the cause (change). Response = what the living thing does.

similar_questions.stem: You smell food and your mouth waters. The smell of food is the
explanation_steps: The smell is the change that causes the response.

questions.stem: If two horizontal forces of 90 N and 45 N are acting on an object in the opposite direction, then the net force is
explanation_steps: When forces act in opposite directions, subtract them.
Net force = 90 N − 45 N = 45 N (in the direction of the 90 N force). Answer: A.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 45)
questions.explain_simple: Opposite forces: 90 − 45 = 45 N.
tips: Same direction: add. Opposite directions: subtract.

similar_questions.stem: Two forces of 30 N and 20 N push a box in the SAME direction. The net force is
explanation_steps: Same direction: 30 + 20 = 50 N.

questions.stem: An object vibrates 50 times in one second. The frequency of the object is:
explanation_steps: Frequency is the number of vibrations in one second.
50 vibrations in one second = 50 Hz. (The textbook uses this same example.) Answer: D.
questions.explain_simple: 50 vibrations each second is 50 Hz.
tips: 1 Hz = 1 vibration per second.

similar_questions.stem: A drum skin vibrates 200 times in 2 seconds. Its frequency is

questions.stem: X, Y and Z in figure 3 are constituents of air in percent. So, constituent Z is
questions.image_alt: Figure 3: pie chart of air. Y = 78% (largest part), X = 21% (dotted part), Z = 1% (thin black slice).
explanation_steps: In the chart, Y = 78% (nitrogen) and X = 21% (oxygen).
Z = 1%. The textbook says the last 1% is carbon dioxide and other gases such as water vapour. Answer: B.
questions.explain_simple: Z is the small 1%. It is carbon dioxide and other gases.
tips: Air: 78% nitrogen, 21% oxygen, 1% carbon dioxide and other gases.

similar_questions.stem: In the same chart, which gas is X (21%)?
explanation_steps: 21% of air is oxygen.

questions.stem: A car changes its speed from 20 m/s to 26 m/s in 2 seconds. The car’s acceleration is:
explanation_steps: Acceleration = (final velocity − initial velocity) ÷ time.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 58)
questions.explain_simple: The speed grows by 6 m/s in 2 s. 6 ÷ 2 = 3 m/s².
tips: a = (v − u) ÷ t.

similar_questions.stem: A runner speeds up from 2 m/s to 6 m/s in 4 s. Her acceleration is

questions.stem: When a copper wire is heated, its length would
explanation_steps: When a solid is heated, its molecules move more and move apart. The solid expands.
So a heated copper wire gets longer. Answer: B.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 117)
questions.explain_simple: Heat makes metals expand. The wire gets longer.
tips: Heat → expand. Cool → contract.

similar_questions.stem: Why do engineers leave small gaps between railway rails?

options.B: so rails can expand in hot weather

explanation_steps: Rails expand when hot. Gaps stop them from bending.

questions.stem: Which one of the following prevents STDs, AIDS, and early age pregnancy 100%?
explanation_steps: The textbook says the best way of preventing STDs, including AIDS, is abstinence from sex. Abstinence is also the best way to prevent pregnancy.
Pills and injections do not protect against STDs. A condom must be used correctly DURING sex, not after. Answer: D.
questions.explain_simple: Not having sex (abstinence) is the only 100% protection.
tips: Abstinence = choosing not to have sex. It is 100% safe.

similar_questions.stem: Which disease is sexually transmitted?
explanation_steps: Syphilis is an STD.

questions.stem: Plant response to water is called
explanation_steps: 'Hydro' means water. A plant growing towards water shows hydrotropism.
Geotropism is response to gravity, thigmotropism to touch, phototropism to light. Answer: A.
(textbook: Science Grade 7, p. 81)
questions.explain_simple: Hydro = water. The response to water is hydrotropism.
tips: hydro = water, geo = gravity, thigmo = touch, photo = light.

similar_questions.stem: A climbing plant twists around a stick. This is
explanation_steps: It is a response to touch: thigmotropism.

questions.stem: Dusting pollen of a tall pea plant to the stigma of a short pea plant by hands is
explanation_steps: Pollination is moving pollen to a stigma. Here the pollen goes from one plant (tall) to a different plant (short): cross pollination.
It is done by hand, so it is artificial. Answer: D.
(textbook: Science Grade 7, p. 205)
questions.explain_simple: Pollen goes by hand from one plant to another: artificial cross pollination.
tips: Same plant = self pollination. Different plant = cross pollination.

similar_questions.stem: Which of these usually carries pollen in natural pollination?
explanation_steps: Insects like bees and the wind carry pollen.

questions.stem: A cell part present in plant cell but absent in animal cell is
explanation_steps: The cell wall surrounds the cell membrane of a plant cell. Animal cells do not have it.
Nucleus, cell membrane and mitochondrion are in both. Answer: A.
(textbook: Science Grade 6, p. 104)
questions.explain_simple: Only plant cells have a cell wall.
tips: Plant only: cell wall, chloroplasts, large vacuole.

similar_questions.stem: Which part gives a plant cell its fixed shape?
explanation_steps: The strong cell wall gives the plant cell its shape.

questions.stem: From the following, identify a pair of acquired traits.

options.A: shape of nose and ability to swim
options.C: shape of nose and ear structure

explanation_steps: Acquired traits are gained during life: a tattoo is made on the body, and swimming is learned.
Shape of nose, eye colour, skin colour and ear structure are inherited. Only D has two acquired traits. Answer: D.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 142)
questions.explain_simple: A tattoo and swimming are both gained during life.
tips: Learned skills and body changes after birth are acquired.

similar_questions.stem: Which is an inherited trait?
explanation_steps: Curly hair comes from the parents' genes.

questions.stem: A human activity that causes soil pollution is
explanation_steps: Pesticides are chemicals. When they are sprayed, some go into the soil and pollute it.
Terracing protects soil; watering and growing vegetables do not pollute. Answer: A.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 191)
questions.explain_simple: Pesticide chemicals get into the soil and pollute it.
tips: Soil pollution: chemicals, plastics, industrial waste.

similar_questions.stem: Which activity helps protect soil?
explanation_steps: Terraces stop water from washing soil away.

textbook_ref.unit: Unit 9 – Human Impact on the Environment

questions.stem: In Figure 4, plate ‘A’ contains fine dry salt and plate ‘B’ contains fine dry sugar. The salt can be identified from the sugar by
questions.image_alt: Figure 4: two plates of fine white powder that look the same. Plate A has salt, plate B has sugar.
explanation_steps: Fine salt and fine sugar look the same. Both have no smell, and both dissolve in water.
But salt tastes salty and sugar tastes sweet. So tasting tells them apart. Answer: A.
(Salt and sugar are foods. Never taste unknown chemicals in a laboratory.)
(textbook: Science Grade 6, p. 40)
questions.explain_simple: Salt is salty and sugar is sweet. Taste them to know.
tips: Taste is a physical property, but only taste things you know are food.

similar_questions.stem: Which property can separate iron filings from sand?
explanation_steps: A magnet attracts iron, not sand.

textbook_ref.unit: Unit 3 – Properties and Changes of Matter

questions.stem: Which one of the following is the SI unit of length?
explanation_steps: The SI unit of length is the metre (m).
Kilogram is mass; hour and second are time. Answer: B.
(textbook: Science Grade 6, p. 8)
questions.explain_simple: Length is measured in metres.
tips: SI: metre, kilogram, second.

similar_questions.stem: Which instrument measures length?
explanation_steps: A metre rule measures length.

questions.stem: Na atom has 11 electrons. So, its last shell contains
explanation_steps: Fill the shells: first shell 2, second shell 8, then 11 − 10 = 1 left.
Sodium is 2, 8, 1. The last shell has one electron. Answer: A.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 79)
questions.explain_simple: Sodium is 2, 8, 1. Its last shell has 1 electron.
tips: Fill shells in order: 2, then 8, then the rest.

similar_questions.stem: Chlorine has 17 electrons. How many are in its last shell?
explanation_steps: 2, 8, 7: seven electrons in the last shell.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a renewable resource?
explanation_steps: Water is renewed again and again by the water cycle, so it is renewable.
Coal and oil are fossil fuels, and gold is a mineral. Once used, they cannot be replaced. Answer: B.
(textbook: Science Grade 7, p. 62)
questions.explain_simple: Water comes back through the water cycle. It is renewable.
tips: Renewable: water, sun, wind, forests. Non-renewable: coal, oil, gas, minerals.

similar_questions.stem: Which is non-renewable?
explanation_steps: Natural gas is a fossil fuel.

questions.stem: Figure 5 below shows a complete circuit of electricity. The sequence of the energy transformation is represented by:
questions.image_alt: Figure 5: a 1.5 V cell, a switch and a glowing bulb joined in a closed circuit by wires.
explanation_steps: The cell (battery) stores chemical energy.
In the circuit, the chemical energy changes to electrical energy, and the bulb changes it to light and heat. Answer: B.
(Options A and C are printed the same; both are wrong.)
(textbook: Science Grade 6, p. 52)
questions.explain_simple: Battery (chemical) → electricity → bulb (light and heat).
tips: Cell: chemical → electrical. Bulb: electrical → light + heat.

similar_questions.stem: A solar panel changes
explanation_steps: A solar panel turns sunlight into electricity.

questions.stem: A person can clearly see far object but cannot see near object. This person is
explanation_steps: The textbook says a person who can see distant objects clearly but cannot see near objects is long sighted.
A short-sighted person sees near things clearly but not far things. Answer: B.
questions.explain_simple: Sees far things well but not near things: long sighted.
tips: Long sight → convex lens. Short sight → concave lens.

similar_questions.stem: Short sight is corrected with
explanation_steps: Short sight needs a concave (diverging) lens.

questions.stem: Fatima slips while she tries to walk on an icy road. This is because

options.A: the friction force between her shoes and the road is low
options.B: the gravitation force between her shoes and the road is high
options.C: the friction force between her shoes and the road is high
options.D: the gravitation force between her shoes and the road is low

explanation_steps: We need friction between our shoes and the ground to walk.
Ice is very smooth, so friction is low. Her shoes slide and she slips. Answer: A.
(textbook: Science Grade 6, p. 28)
questions.explain_simple: Ice is smooth, so there is little friction. That is why she slips.
tips: Smooth surface → low friction → slipping.

similar_questions.stem: Why do car tyres have deep patterns (treads)?
explanation_steps: Treads increase friction so the tyres grip the road.

questions.stem: Edible grains like wheat, barley and sorghum are examples of
explanation_steps: Cereals are grass-like crops that give edible grains: wheat, barley, sorghum, maize, teff.
Oil seeds give oil (e.g. sesame); fibre crops give fibre (e.g. cotton). Answer: D.
(textbook: Science Grade 7, p. 109)
questions.explain_simple: Wheat, barley and sorghum are cereal crops.
tips: Cereals = grains. Pulses = beans, peas. Oil seeds = sesame, sunflower.

similar_questions.stem: Which is an oil seed crop?
explanation_steps: Sesame seeds are used to make oil.

questions.stem: The layer of an atmosphere preferable by airplane pilots to fly is:
explanation_steps: The textbook says pilots like to fly in the stratosphere because there is little weather there.
Clouds, rain and storms happen in the troposphere below. Answer: A.
questions.explain_simple: Pilots fly in the stratosphere. It has little weather.
tips: Troposphere: weather. Stratosphere: ozone layer, calm air for planes.

similar_questions.stem: The ozone layer is found in the
explanation_steps: The stratosphere contains the ozone layer.

questions.stem: The speed of sound in air is about 330 m/s. How long does it take to travel 1650 m?
explanation_steps: Time = distance ÷ speed.
t = 1650 m ÷ 330 m/s = 5 s. Answer: B.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 208)
tips: time = distance ÷ speed. Time is in seconds (s), not metres.

similar_questions.stem: Sound travels at 340 m/s. How long does it take to travel 680 m?

questions.stem: Mehari pushed a box by exerting a force of 40 N to a distance of 4 m. How much work did he do?
explanation_steps: Work = force × distance.
W = 40 N × 4 m = 160 J. Answer: D.
(textbook: Science Grade 7, p. 59)
tips: Work (J) = force (N) × distance (m).

similar_questions.stem: A girl lifts a bag with a force of 50 N through 2 m. The work done is

questions.stem: Water which is clear to the eye can be made safe to drink by:
explanation_steps: Clear water can still have germs that we cannot see.
Decanting and filtration remove dirt that we can see, but they do not kill germs.
Chlorine kills micro-organisms, so chlorination makes clear water safe to drink. Answer: C.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 182)
questions.explain_simple: Chlorine kills germs, so the water becomes safe.
tips: Remove dirt: decant, filter. Kill germs: boil, chlorinate.

similar_questions.stem: Which method removes mud from water but does NOT kill germs?
explanation_steps: Filtration removes solid bits only.

questions.stem: When bleeding occurs because of skin injury, which cells help in blood clotting?
explanation_steps: Platelets help blood to clot at a cut, so the bleeding stops.
Red cells carry oxygen, white cells fight germs, plasma is the liquid part. Answer: D.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 18)
questions.explain_simple: Platelets help stop bleeding.
tips: Platelets → clotting.

similar_questions.stem: Which part of blood fights germs?
explanation_steps: White blood cells defend the body against germs.

questions.stem: Three human organs and their functions are given in Table 1. They are parts of the
explanation_steps: The nose, trachea and lungs are the organs of breathing.
They make up the respiratory system. Answer: D.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 11)
questions.explain_simple: Nose, trachea and lungs belong to the respiratory system.
tips: Respiratory: nose → trachea → bronchi → lungs (alveoli).

similar_questions.stem: Which organ is part of the digestive system?
explanation_steps: The stomach digests food.

questions.stem: A student measured the temperature of a class room using a Celsius thermometer as shown in figure 6 below. The temperature of the class room in °C is:
questions.image_alt: Figure 6: a Celsius thermometer from 0 to 40 °C, big marks every 5 °C and small marks every 1 °C. The liquid column ends 2 small marks above 25.
explanation_steps: The big marks are every 5 °C (0, 5, 10, … 40). Between two big marks there are small marks for each 1 °C.
The top of the liquid is 2 small marks above 25.
So the reading is 25 + 2 = 27 °C. Answer: A.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 121)
questions.explain_simple: The liquid is 2 marks above 25. That is 27 °C.
tips: Find the value of one small mark first, then count.

similar_questions.stem: On a thermometer the big marks are 10, 20, 30 and there are 10 small marks between them. The liquid is 4 small marks above 20. The reading is
explanation_steps: Each small mark is 1 °C, so 20 + 4 = 24 °C.

questions.stem: Sulphur + Oxygen → Sulphur dioxide. In this word equation, identify the product(s).
explanation_steps: In an equation the reactants are on the left of the arrow and the products are on the right.
Sulphur dioxide is on the right, so it is the product. Answer: D.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 90)
questions.explain_simple: Sulphur dioxide is made in the reaction. It is the product.
tips: Reactants → products.

similar_questions.stem: In the same equation, what are the reactants?
explanation_steps: The substances on the left are the reactants.

textbook_ref.unit: Unit 4 – Chemical Reactions and the Periodic Table

questions.stem: An example of heterogeneous mixture is
explanation_steps: In a heterogeneous mixture you can see the different parts.
Soil has sand, clay, small stones and bits of plants that you can see. It is a heterogeneous mixture.
Salt and sugar are compounds and oxygen is an element; they are pure substances, not mixtures. Answer: C.
(textbook: Science Grade 7, p. 44)
questions.explain_simple: Soil has many parts you can see. It is a heterogeneous mixture.
tips: Can you see different parts? → heterogeneous.

similar_questions.stem: Which is a homogeneous mixture?
explanation_steps: Salt water looks the same everywhere.

questions.stem: An empty balloon weighs 5 g but when it is filled with air, it weighs 5.1 g. Therefore,
explanation_steps: The balloon became heavier (5 g → 5.1 g) when air was added. So the air inside has mass (weight).
Air has no definite volume or shape. 'Air occupies space' is also true, but the weighing shows mass. Answer: C.
(textbook: Science Grade 6, p. 85)
questions.explain_simple: The balloon got heavier with air. So air has mass.
tips: Weighing shows mass. A balloon getting bigger shows air takes up space.

similar_questions.stem: A bottle with a balloon on top is put in hot water, and the balloon grows. This shows that air
explanation_steps: Heated air expands and fills the balloon.

questions.review_flag: Wording: the weighing shows that air has mass (C is keyed), but the option says 'definite mass', which is odd for a gas. Option B 'air occupies space' is also a true property of air and is shown by the balloon filling up. Keyed C; a teacher may also accept B.

questions.stem: Convert a temperature of 68 °F to degree Celsius:
explanation_steps: (textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 122)

similar_questions.stem: Convert 86 °F to °C.

questions.stem: The method of heat transfer that occurs in solids is
explanation_steps: In solids, heat passes from particle to particle. This is conduction.
Convection happens in liquids and gases; radiation needs no medium; insulation stops heat. Answer: A.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 106)
questions.explain_simple: In solids heat moves by conduction.
tips: Solids: conduction. Liquids and gases: convection. Empty space: radiation.

similar_questions.stem: Heat from the sun reaches the earth by
explanation_steps: Only radiation can pass through empty space.

questions.stem: The type of cell division that occurs in body cells is
explanation_steps: The textbook says mitosis occurs only in body cells.
Meiosis makes sex cells. A zygote is a fertilized egg, and variation means differences; neither is cell division. Answer: B.
questions.explain_simple: Body cells divide by mitosis.
tips: Mitosis → body cells. Meiosis → sex cells.

similar_questions.stem: A fertilized egg is called a
explanation_steps: When sperm and egg join, they form a zygote.

questions.stem: Which of the following is correct? The speed of sound in

options.A: liquids is less than in gases
options.B: gases is greater than in solids
options.C: solids is greater than in liquids
options.D: solids is less than in gases

explanation_steps: Sound travels fastest in solids, slower in liquids, and slowest in gases.
So the speed in solids is greater than in liquids. Answer: C.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 208)
questions.explain_simple: Sound is fastest in solids.
tips: Speed of sound: solids > liquids > gases.

similar_questions.stem: You put your ear on a railway line and hear a train before you hear it through the air. Why?

options.B: sound is faster in the steel rail

explanation_steps: Sound travels faster through solids like steel.

questions.stem: If an organism’s sex cell contains 28 chromosomes, its body cell has
explanation_steps: A sex cell has half the number of chromosomes of a body cell.
Body cell = 2 × 28 = 56 chromosomes. Answer: A.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 134)
questions.explain_simple: The body cell has double: 28 × 2 = 56.
tips: Body cell = 2 × sex cell.

similar_questions.stem: A body cell has 46 chromosomes. A sperm cell of the same person has

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a function of the human skeleton?
explanation_steps: The skeleton protects organs, supports the body and allows movement (with muscles).
Oxygen is supplied by the lungs and the blood, not by the skeleton. Answer: C.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 29)
questions.explain_simple: The skeleton does not supply oxygen.
tips: Skeleton: support, shape, protection, movement.

similar_questions.stem: Which bones protect the heart and lungs?
explanation_steps: The rib cage protects the heart and lungs.

questions.stem: In figure 7, the simple machine that is categorized as a 2nd order lever is:
questions.image_alt: Figure 7: four tools – pliers, a wheelbarrow, scissors and a claw hammer.
explanation_steps: In a second-class lever the load is between the fulcrum and the effort.
In a wheelbarrow the wheel is the fulcrum, the load is in the middle, and you lift the handles (effort).
Pliers and scissors are first-class levers; a claw hammer pulling a nail is also first-class. Answer: B.
(textbook: Science Grade 7, p. 13)
questions.explain_simple: In a wheelbarrow the load is in the middle. It is a second-class lever.
tips: 1st class: fulcrum in middle. 2nd class: load in middle. 3rd class: effort in middle.

similar_questions.stem: Which is a second-class lever?
explanation_steps: The textbook lists the bottle opener as a second-class lever.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an opaque material?
explanation_steps: Opaque materials do not let light pass through.
Glass and water are transparent. Oiled paper is translucent (some light passes).
A mirror reflects light and does not let it through, so it is opaque. Answer: C.
(textbook: Science Grade 6, p. 65)
questions.explain_simple: Light cannot pass through a mirror. It is opaque.
tips: Transparent: all light passes. Translucent: some. Opaque: none.

similar_questions.stem: Which material is translucent?
explanation_steps: Oiled paper lets some light through.

questions.stem: The ability of living things to react to environmental changes is their
explanation_steps: The textbook says the ability to react to changes in the environment is called sensitivity.
A stimulus is the change itself; receptors and effectors are body parts. Answer: C.
questions.explain_simple: Reacting to changes is called sensitivity.
tips: Sensitivity = ability to respond. Stimulus = the change.

similar_questions.stem: Which part in the body detects a stimulus?
explanation_steps: Receptors detect changes.

questions.stem: In figure 8, what do the arrows represent?
questions.image_alt: Figure 8: food chain – plant → grasshopper → frog → hawk.

options.A: energy transfer from organism to organism

explanation_steps: The figure is a food chain: plant → grasshopper → frog → hawk.
A food chain shows how energy passes from one organism to the next when one eats another. The arrows show this energy transfer. Answer: A.
(textbook: Science Grade 7, p. 128)
questions.explain_simple: The arrows show energy passing from the eaten to the eater.
tips: In a food chain the arrow points to the eater.

similar_questions.stem: In the chain plant → grasshopper → frog → hawk, which is the producer?
explanation_steps: The plant makes its own food.

questions.stem: Sources of water can be kept clean by

options.A: urinating into the sources of water
options.B: defecating in the sources of water
options.C: throwing rubbish into sources of water
options.D: protecting contamination of sources of water

explanation_steps: Urine, faeces and rubbish make water dirty and spread disease.
We keep water clean by protecting it from contamination. Answer: D.
(textbook: Science Grade 8, p. 177)
questions.explain_simple: Keep dirt and waste away from water.
tips: Protect wells and rivers: no waste near water sources.

similar_questions.stem: Which disease can spread from water polluted by human waste?
explanation_steps: Cholera spreads through water dirty with human waste.

questions.stem: In Table 2, a ‘√’ means ‘produces’. So, light energy is produced by:
explanation_steps: Look at the 'Light' column of the table.
Only burning wood and the sun have a tick under Light. Answer: B.
(textbook: Science Grade 6, p. 52)
questions.explain_simple: In the table, burning wood and the sun make light.
tips: Read down the right column and find the ticks.

similar_questions.stem: According to Table 2, which source produces sound?
explanation_steps: Only the drum has a tick under Sound.

questions.stem: What fraction of the earth’s surface is covered by water?
explanation_steps: The textbook says water covers nearly three-quarters of the earth's surface.
Three-quarters = 3/4. Answer: C.
questions.explain_simple: Water covers about 3/4 of the earth.
tips: 3/4 water, 1/4 land.

similar_questions.stem: What fraction of the earth's surface is land?
explanation_steps: If water is about 3/4, land is about 1/4.
